# Quote Submission Form

> Complete this form for every quote you send in. A quote is the shortest piece
> of content NHECOF publishes, which makes it the easiest to get wrong: one
> invented quotation, or one unattributed health claim, is enough to damage
> trust in everything else.
>
> **This form is what you fill in and send to the content manager or reviewer.
> It is not the Studio form.** The person who enters it into Sanity will
> transcribe your answers into `Content → Quote → +`.

---

## Part 1 — The quote

**1. The quote text**

> Plain text only. No quotation marks around it — the website adds those.
> Maximum 220 characters including spaces and punctuation. Count it.

_______________________________________________

_______________________________________________

**Character count** (must be 220 or fewer): ________

- [ ] Under 220 characters
- [ ] Makes complete sense on its own, with no surrounding context needed
- [ ] No claim that food cures, treats, heals or prevents anything
- [ ] Not a near-copy of something already on the site
- [ ] Not something AI generated (see the box below)

> **AI-generated quotes are not accepted.** A quote may be *inspired* or
> *written from scratch by a person*, but a health statement produced by a
> chatbot and presented as NHECOF's own thinking is not something we publish.
> If a tool helped you phrase it, that is fine — but a human being must have
> written the idea and stand behind it as true. Write the quote yourself.

**2. Is this quote attributed to a named person, or to NHECOF?**

☐ Attributed to a named person → go to Part 2
☐ Attributed to `NHECOF` → go to Part 3
☐ Attributed to another organisation or publication → go to Part 2

---

## Part 2 — Attribution

**3. Who said it?**

**Full name:** _______________________________________________

**Role or title** (e.g. "Nutritionist, NHECOF"): ______________

**Are they happy to be named?**

☐ Yes, in writing, and I have the permission ☐ Not certain — do not publish yet

> If the answer is not certain, the quote is not ready. An unnamed person who
> turns out not to have agreed is a problem NHECOF cannot fix afterwards.

**4. If the quote came from somewhere else, where?**

☐ This is the person's own words — no source needed
☐ Quoted from a publication, speech, report or other organisation

If quoted from elsewhere:

**Original source title:** _______________________________________

**Publisher:** _______________________________________________

**Web address** (if there is one): _______________________________

**Date of the original** (if known): ______________

> **If you cannot say where it came from, it is not a quotation — it is
> something somebody said.** Use Part 3 and attribute it to NHECOF instead.

**5. If the quote is a health statement, where is the evidence?**

> A quote that makes a specific health claim needs a source, just like an
> article does. Name the authority that supports it.

_______________________________________________

**Suggested authority** (WHO, Federal Ministry of Health, UNICEF, a published
study, and so on): _______________________________________

- [ ] The claim is supported by a source I can name
- [ ] I have read that source and it supports this specific wording
      *(if no — reword the quote to be more modest and try again)*

---

## Part 3 — Where and when to show it

**6. Topic**

☐ Nutrition ☐ Healthy living ☐ Maternal health ☐ Child nutrition
☐ Food safety ☐ General wellness

**7. Display dates**

☐ Evergreen — show it all year *(leave both dates empty)*
☐ Seasonal or campaign — set the dates below

**Display start date:** ______________ (`YYYY-MM-DD`)
**Display end date:** ______________ (`YYYY-MM-DD`, or leave empty for ever)

- [ ] Start date is not in the past unless I want it to start immediately
- [ ] End date is after the start date
- [ ] I understand that if a scheduled quote is not approved, a different quote
      appears that day instead, with no warning

**8. Social sharing permission**

☐ Yes — this quote may appear on social sharing cards
☐ No — do not put it on social media cards

> If the quote names a member of the public, a patient, a volunteer or a
> beneficiary, or comes from another organisation, the answer is almost
> always **No**.

**9. Active**

☐ Active — eligible to be shown
☐ Inactive — do not show (e.g. it is being rewritten)

---

## Part 4 — Handover

**10. Who is reviewing this quote?**

**Reviewer name:** _______________________________________________

- [ ] A qualified reviewer has agreed to check it — *not* the person who wrote it

**11. Who is entering it into the Studio?**

**Name:** ______________  **Date:** ______________

**12. For the person entering it in the Studio**

- [ ] `text` — copied exactly, no added quotation marks
- [ ] `attribution` — filled in, including `NHECOF` if that is the attribution
- [ ] `sourceUrl` — only if the quote genuinely came from a source
- [ ] `topic` — one of the seven listed values
- [ ] `active` — set correctly
- [ ] `reviewStatus` — **Submitted for Review**, not left on Draft
- [ ] `sharingPermitted` — set explicitly, every time
- [ ] `startDate` / `endDate` — set, if a window was requested

> **Important:** a quote that is still on `Draft` will never appear on the
> website, even if everything else is right. The website only ever shows quotes
> that are both **Approved** and **Active**.

---

- [ ] 220 characters or fewer, and I counted
- [ ] Makes sense on its own
- [ ] Attribution is accurate and the person agreed
- [ ] Source named, if it came from someone else
- [ ] Any health claim is supported by a source I can point to
- [ ] No cure / treat / heal / prevent / guarantee language
- [ ] I wrote it myself, it was not generated by AI
- [ ] `sharingPermitted` decided deliberately
- [ ] A qualified reviewer has agreed to check it
